verdict: Hormel's sales slipped 2% to $3.0 billion and reported profit fell by two-thirds, but almost all of the damage was one-time charges — while the underlying food business raised its full-year outlook.

segments.name: Retail
segments.note: Grocery brands like SPAM, Applegate, Planters and Hormel chili — sales fell 4% and volume fell 9% on weak commodity turkey and private-label snack nuts.

segments.name: Foodservice
segments.note: Selling to restaurants and institutions — a 12th straight quarter of organic sales growth, led by premium prepared proteins and pepperoni.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Sales outside the U.S. — the segment swung to a $29M loss from a $19M profit, hit by the portfolio reshaping described below.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing, offices and running the company.

opex.name: Equity loss in affiliates
opex.note: Hormel's share of losses from businesses it part-owns — a swing from an $11M profit a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest income of $6.7M and $5.2M of other income, less $19.6M of interest expense — net −$7.7M.
footerNote: Figures are converted from the release's thousands and rounded to one decimal in $M; net earnings of $59.5M are the total, of which $59.6M was attributable to Hormel Foods after a small noncontrolling-interest loss. The quarter's effective tax rate was an unusually high 42.3%, distorted by the one-time items.

takeaways.title: The gap is one-time charges
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income was $111 million; adjusted operating income was $266 million. The roughly $155 million gap is mostly one-time items — the Brazil divestiture, an impairment in Indonesia, and a litigation settlement.

takeaways.title: Retail volume is the worry
takeaways.text: Retail volume fell 9% as shoppers and commodity pricing worked against turkey and snack nuts — though SPAM, Applegate and Hormel chili grew. Management still cut the full-year sales outlook to $12.1–12.2 billion.

takeaways.title: Foodservice keeps delivering
takeaways.text: Foodservice segment profit rose 3% to $144 million on its 12th straight quarter of organic sales growth — the steadiest part of the business while retail struggles.

oneTimers: GAAP results include one-time items that Hormel's adjusted results strip out: an estimated loss on the Brazil divestiture, a non-cash impairment charge on a minority investment in Indonesia, and a litigation settlement.
Equity in earnings of affiliates swung to a $37M loss from an $11M profit a year ago, another drag on the GAAP line.
The quarter's 42.3% effective tax rate (vs 22.3% a year ago) is distorted by these items and is not a guide to future quarters.
